description: Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol No and atomic number 102, named after Alfred Nobel. It is a radioactive metal that is the tenth transuranium element, the second transfermium, and the fourteenth member of the actinide series. It can only be produced in particle accelerators by bombarding lighter elements with charged particles.
uses: Nobelium is used in chemistry experiments to study the behavior of heavier homologs in the periodic table. The isotope 255No is most commonly used in chemistry because it can be produced on a larger scale, despite shorter-lived isotopes existing.
characteristics: Nobelium is a radioactive metal with twelve known isotopes; the most stable is 259No with a half-life of 58 minutes. It behaves as a heavier homolog to ytterbium and exhibits a stable +2 oxidation state in aqueous solution, which is much more stable than the +3 state characteristic of other actinides. Nobelium metal has not yet been prepared in bulk quantities, and bulk preparation is currently impossible.
